what: Exelon is the largest electricity delivery company in the United States. It does not generate power: it owns six regulated utilities that deliver electricity and gas, including ComEd in Chicago, PECO in Philadelphia, BGE in Baltimore and Pepco in Washington.
customers: About 10.7 million households and businesses in Illinois, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Delaware, New Jersey and Washington DC.
money: transmission and distribution across six utilities
gas distribution in several of those territories
moat: Pure delivery monopolies with no exposure to power prices, so earnings depend on regulated returns rather than commodity markets.
risks: Debt of about $49 billion against under $1 billion of cash
Illinois and Maryland regulators have pushed back on requested returns
Heavy capital spending requires regular share issuance
opportunities: Data centre connection requests in Chicago and northern Virginia raise long-term investment needs
Having no generation means no exposure to power price swings
watch: Rate case outcomes and data centre load growth in its territories.
